title: Regional throttle matrix & queueing data pull (March 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This sheet is a focused, exportable data pull to support postmortem analysis for the capacity incidents on 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-07 that impacted hosted API latency and resulted in customer throttles by region. The objective is to produce a compact CSV-ready matrix with both per-region and per-cluster indicators for saturation, queue length, throttle events, and pre/post mitigation comparisons.

Scope & timeframe:
- Window: 2026-03-04 00:00 UTC through 2026-03-08 23:59 UTC (48 hours before first incident -> 48 hours after last mitigation)
- Entities: all GPU clusters serving hosted inference (clusters tagged: gpu-prod-*) across regions (us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1, ap-southeast1)
- Metrics included: GPU_util_pct, queue_len_running, avg_latency_ms, token_throttle_count, api_error_5xx_count, instance_restarts, active_request_rate_rps

Primary deliverable (CSV columns):
- date_hour (YYYY-MM-DDTHH), region, cluster_name, rack_id, instance_type, gpu_count, gpu_util_percent_avg, gpu_util_percent_p95, queue_len_mean, queue_len_p95, avg_response_ms, p95_response_ms, token_throttle_total, throttle_rate_per_1k_requests, error_5xx_total, throttle_policy_version, autoscale_event_count, prefetch_kv_cache_hit_rate, notes

Queries / extraction notes (reference SQL templates to run against metrics warehouse):
- Metric sources: metrics.prod.metrics_v2 (timeseries), traces.request_span, events.throttle_log, infra.instance_events
- Example (Timescale/Postgres-ish):
  -- aggregate GPU utilization per cluster per hour
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', t.ts) AS date_hour, c.region, c.cluster_name, c.rack_id, c.instance_type,
         c.gpu_count,
         avg(t.gpu_util) AS gpu_util_percent_avg,
         percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY t.gpu_util) AS gpu_util_percent_p95
  FROM metrics.prod.metrics_v2 t
  JOIN infra.clusters c ON t.cluster_id = c.id
  WHERE t.ts >= '2026-03-04' AND t.ts < '2026-03-09'
    AND c.cluster_name LIKE 'gpu-prod-%'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6;

  -- queue length, latency, and request-rate by cluster/hour
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', r.ts) AS date_hour, c.region, c.cluster_name,
         avg(r.queue_len) AS queue_len_mean, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY r.queue_len) AS queue_len_p95,
         avg(r.latency_ms) AS avg_response_ms, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY r.latency_ms) AS p95_response_ms,
         sum(r.requests) AS request_count, (sum(r.requests)::float / 3600) AS active_request_rate_rps
  FROM traces.request_span r
  JOIN infra.clusters c ON r.cluster_id = c.id
  WHERE r.ts >= '2026-03-04' AND r.ts < '2026-03-09'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3;

  -- throttles & policies (event log)
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', e.ts) AS date_hour, c.region, c.cluster_name,
         sum(CASE WHEN e.type = 'token_throttle' THEN e.count ELSE 0 END) AS token_throttle_total,
         max(e.throttle_policy_version) AS throttle_policy_version,
         count(DISTINCT e.autoscale_event_id) AS autoscale_event_count
  FROM events.throttle_log e
  JOIN infra.clusters c ON e.cluster_id = c.id
  WHERE e.ts >= '2026-03-04' AND e.ts < '2026-03-09'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3;

Join these three extracts by date_hour+region+cluster_name to produce the matrix. For convenience, add a derived field throttle_rate_per_1k_requests = (token_throttle_total / NULLIF(request_count,0)) * 1000.

Flags + anomaly heuristics to mark rows for quick triage (add as notes column):
- saturation_flag: gpu_util_percent_p95 >= 92% AND gpu_util_percent_avg >= 80%
- persistent_queue_flag: queue_len_p95 >= 15 for >= 3 contiguous hours in the window
- throttle_burst_flag: token_throttle_total >= 1000 in an hour or throttle_rate_per_1k_requests >= 5
- error_spike_flag: error_5xx_total increased >= 3x baseline (baseline = avg of 7 days prior same hour)
- autoscale_mismatch: autoscale_event_count = 0 AND saturation_flag = true AND cluster autoscale_enabled = true (join cluster config table)

Preliminary observations (notes inserted while running live pulls):
- us-west1: multiple clusters show repeated p95 GPU util at ~95% during the incident hours; queue_len_p95 spiked to 38 for cluster gpu-prod-west-12 at 2026-03-05T15:00Z. Throttle events for the cluster started ~15 minutes after queue spike.
- eu-west1: lower token_throttle_total overall but several short 5xx error bursts coincident with failover of two instances (see infra.instance_events).
- ap-southeast1: sustained moderate GPU util (avg 70-82%) but queue_len_p95 rare; appears capacity limit was reached for specific instance types (a2-highgpu variants) during traffic bursts.

Known caveats / data quality checks:
- Metrics ingestion lag: metrics.prod has known 2–10s ingestion lag; for this data pull we accept up to 60s tolerances but annotate any hours with missing data points >2% as "incomplete" in notes.
- Throttle logs are emitted by the gateway and may be delayed during high-error periods; cross-validate with gateway access logs (traces.gateway_access) if throttle counts look inconsistent with request volumes.
- Pre/post mitigation markers: include column mitigation_tag when manual mitigation was applied (e.g., manual_scale, rollback, routing-change). Populate from events.incident_actions table.

Synthesized short summary (to paste into postmortem):
- Root cause signal: high percentile GPU saturation (p95 >= 92%) in us-west1 clusters plus queuing spikes that preceded token throttle enforcement. Autoscaler did not trigger scaling fast enough for a subset of clusters due to conservative cooldown settings and a missing instance pool in us-west1-2.
- Impact vector: elevated queue_backlog increased request latency and led to token-based throttles on the gateway as a protective measure; customers in us-west1 and a subset in eu-west1 observed elevated 5xx rates and increased latency.
- Immediate mitigations applied: manual_scale up of 8 GPU instances in affected clusters, temporary increase in throttle thresholds for specific customers, and emergency routing to dedicated capacity in us-east4.

Recommended follow-ups (action items for infra + serving runtime):
1) Add an autoscale precondition check: if p95 GPU util > 90% for 2 consecutive hours AND queue_len_p95 > 10, trigger aggressive scale (bypass cooldown).
2) Create a cross-region instance pool failover plan for high-demand instance types (a2 variants).
3) Update throttle policy to emit an early-warning event when throttle_rate_per_1k_requests > 1 for any 3-hour window.
4) Run a targeted load test for us-west1 clusters with realistic token distributions and KV cache miss ratios.

Appendix A — suggested CSV sample (first 5 rows example):

Notes for the person running the pull:
- Use the time window precisely; we want the hour-granularity matrix for the postmortem. Keep raw extracts for 5-minute resolution in a separate archive if someone needs deeper analysis.
- When you join request_count into the main matrix, ensure you carry a null-safe division for throttle rate.
- Flag and export rows with any of the heuristics above to a separate sheet called "triage_flagged_rows.csv" for SRE/SE review.

Contact & ownership: 
- Data pull owner: Priya Desai (eng-infrastructure) — ping in #infra-capacity and @PriyaDesai on Slack.
- If you find a mismatch between throttle logs and gateway access logs, escalate to Ethan Cole (obs) and Marta Ivanova (serving-runtime) for cross-verification.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-08: initial draft and SQL templates (Priya D.)
- 2026-03-10: added preliminary observations and sample CSV rows after first pass extraction (Priya D., Ethan C.)

End of sheet.
